boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Stirling's Plantation record (September 29, 1863) in Taylor's Operations in West Louisiana [June-September 1863]. The live campaign label reads Taylor's Operations in Louisiana West of Mississip[pi]. Green's Atchafalaya crossing on September 28-30 is context. Campaign-wide movements (Major's raid, the capture of Brashear City and Bayou Boeuf, the river batteries of July 3-10, the withdrawal to the Teche and the September operations) and multi-action totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 2nd Division, XIII Army Corps [US] and forces on the Atchafalaya River [CS]; the live field reads zero. NPS says a 1,000-man detachment under Leake was at Stirling's Plantation; Irwin says Herron's division at Morganza was about 2,500 strong. Green names Speight's and Mouton's brigades, Waller's and Rountree's battalions, Semmes's battery and three dismounted Texas regiments without numbers.
claims.rationale: Figures for different scopes (detachment and division) from a summary and a history; no Confederate count. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 575 total (US 454; CS 121); the live field reads 636 total (US 515; CS 121). Green reports 433 enlisted and 29 officer prisoners and a loss totalling 121 in his inclosure. Irwin says Green killed 16, wounded 45 and took 454 prisoners, and gives Green's loss as 26 killed, 85 wounded and 10 missing, printed as 212 in all although those figures sum to 121.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Irwin's printed 212 does not match his components and is preserved as printed.

open_questions: Banks's No. 1 (read), Dana's No. 2, Bruce's No. 3 and the Second Division record of events (No. 4), Mouton's No. 5 with Taylor's indorsement (read, not selected), the subordinate Confederate reports and the Union returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Richard B. Irwin's History of the Nineteenth Army Corps (Putnam's, 1892), already registered for the Red River pass, is an interested Union history by the corps' assistant adjutant-general. Its chapters cite and quote Stickney's and Green's reports, so it is not independent of them. Green's June 27 dispatch and July 3, July 14 and October 2, 1863 reports, with his undated casualty statement (Official Records Series I, Volume XXVI, Part 1, a shared container), are one interested Confederate family; Taylor's printed indorsements are not part of it. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
